metadata.methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using a Nihon Kohden EEG 2100 clinical device with 19 scalp electrodes (10-20 system) plus 2 mastoid electrodes, sampled at 500 Hz. Participants were seated with eyes open while exposed to photic stimulation at incremental frequencies from 5 Hz up to 30 Hz. Preprocessing included a 0.5-45 Hz Butterworth band-pass filter, re-referencing to A1-A2, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR) for artifact correction, and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) with automatic classification (ICLabel) to remove eye and jaw artifact components.

We explore the key areas that researchers and engineers must consider when developing a deep learning model for biosensing: the data modality, the model architecture, and the real-world use case for the model. In contrast, fractal dimension and long-range temporal correlations (LRTCs) revealed distinct topographical differences: AD exhibited rostral dominance in fractal dimension, whereas FTD showed caudal dominance. citation_details.abstract: Photostimulation-evoked neural entrainment represents a largely unexplored paradigm for differential dementia phenotyping, extending beyond conventional resting-state neurophysiology. We present a multidomain approach that integrates SSVEP biomarkers with spectral and connectivity dynamics for pathophysiology-specific dementia characterization. Through the analysis of 88 participants (36 Alzheimer’s disease, 23 frontotemporal dementia, 29 healthy controls) using EEG, we demonstrate significant dementia differentiation with our top biomarker showing strong group differences (theta-alpha ratio: F = 10.09, p2= 0.192), revealing elevated spectral ratios in both patient groups compared to healthy controls. Our approach identifies 15 discriminative biomarkers spanning 8 frequency-domain spectral ratios, 2 inter-regional connectivity measures, and 5 stimulus-locked entrainment features, contributing toward controlled neurophysiological assessment in neurodegenerative disease stratification.
